results.name: setup: project 481 (Koblenz) is moved into Frankfurt by A's account, so Frankfurt-only B may see it
auth: server-verified identities — no token = login page; no claims = no workspace access; B sees only Frankfurt
both browsers open the real Projekte page (server pages, no data.json, no whole-dataset download)
PROOF 1: A edits Projektstand of 481 → server commits N+1 → audit + outbox + relay → B's table changes, no reload
ITEM 2: A creates a project → B (online) gets it via the event-triggered targeted list refresh, no reload
ITEM 2: A(editor) is denied delete; an admin deletes it → B's row disappears by targeted removal, no reload
PROOF 2: B goes offline; A changes 481 three times in the UI; B reconnects and converges exactly to server state
PROOF 3a: A and B edit the same field concurrently → A commits, B gets the structured conflict, nobody is overwritten; B keeps the server value
PROOF 3b: same race → B explicitly chooses 'mine' → committed as the next version, A sees it live, audit chain intact
PROOF 4: A moves 481 Frankfurt → Kassel; Frankfurt-only B loses the row and receives no Kassel state (stream + DOM + API)
PROOF 5: B offline; A creates a project, deletes one, moves one out, moves one in; B reconnects and its table equals the authoritative visible collection
integrity: every committed change has exactly one audit set, one event, one feedSeq; feed is gapless; nothing unpublished/dead
